newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan pharmaceuticals seen having bright future.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan pharmaceuticals seen having bright future.

text.p: Pharmaceutical firms are seen to have a bright future on Pakistan's depressed stock market, a research report by Kausar Abbas Bhayani Securities Ltd said on Tuesday.
"The future looks bright for the listed pharmaceutical units," said the report prepared by Zubair Elahi, Ali Raza Mooney and Asif Janmohammad of the company.
At present 15 companies are quoted on the Karachi Stock Exchange (KSE) with a listed capital of 1.39 billion rupees, it said.
The report said the market capitalisation of these units was 12.72 billion, or 2.69 percent of the total market capitalisation on September 30.
Most of the pharmaceutical units continued to grow at a fairly rapid rate, Elahi said.

"Almost all the pharma companies quoted at the KSE have shared profit, for the year 1995, with the stockholders. The average payout for the industry for this particular year comes to an admirable 44.28 percent," he said.
"Highest dividend being declared by Parke Davis, 160 percent (per 10-rupee share) cash," Elahi said.
Pharmaceutical companies had become synonymous with high profits, he added.
"Aided by the nature of their products as well as excellent management, these companies will continue to post higher profits," Ali Raza Mooney said.

He said the shares of the industry were not freely traded, because of a thin capital base, with over 50 percent of issued capital with the parent company. Institutions also tended to hold the stocks over a longer term, he said.
"The financial strength of the listed pharma units has increased by leaps and bounds", Mooney said.
Despite showing record profits these companies were trading at low levels due to a depressed stock market, Janmohammad said.
Sizable capital gains could be reaped whenever the market again turned bullish, Janmohammad said.
Parke-Davis 10-rupee stock closed 1.00 rupee down at 676 on Monday from Sunday. Knoll Pharmaceuticals closed 1.00 down at 126.
Pakistan has 301 licensed pharmaceutical units including 31 multinational pharmaceutical companies.
